title: Adjacent quotient squares of the fixed finite tensor shifts
statement: For every prime l, finite extension E of Q_l and scheme W in the same universe, the explicit first- and second-factor finite tensor shifts [def-pod-tensor-finite-signed-shifts] satisfy PodTensorFiniteShiftTransitions: for every adjacent quotient level n, cochain complexes P,Q and integer r, the tensor transition at the shifted input followed by the level-n shift equals the level-(n+1) shift followed by the shifted tensor transition at (P,Q). These are equalities of the concrete chain maps, with no existentially chosen shifts.

source.place: Steps 1 and 5; signed shifts of the same representative-normalized tensor operation. Supporting calculation: Stacks homology.tex, definition-shift-cochain, and more-algebra.tex, item-shift-tensor; descent: sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-pullback-tensor-product.

proof.text: Evaluate both paths on a homogeneous pure tensor. Ordinary coefficient reduction commutes with shifts because its two shifted components have the same scalar-extension generator formula; uniqueness of the reduction transition proves that equality. Then apply the defining tensor-transition formula. The first-factor shift only relabels the summand. The second-factor shift contributes (-1)^(p*r) on both paths, since coefficient reduction is linear and p is unchanged. Local pure tensor generation and direct-sum coproduct extensionality imply equality in every degree; cochain-map extensionality finishes.
